# Arpelio

> Free fingering charts and printable quiz worksheets for band instruments.
> Built for band directors, elementary music teachers, and private lesson
> teachers. No account, no paywall, no download limit.

Arpelio covers 7 instruments across 239 individually verified notes. For every
note it holds the primary fingering, common alternates, whether it is a
first-year "beginner note", common student errors, and practice tips. Fingerings
are checked against professional method books and manufacturer charts.

The site does two things:

1. **Browse fingering charts** — every note and octave for an instrument, with
   alternates and teaching notes.
2. **Build printable worksheets** — pick an instrument and a set of notes, then
   print one of three sheets: a reference chart, an "identify the note" quiz, or
   a "fill the blank diagram" quiz. Quizzes can print a teacher answer key.

## Instruments

- [Recorder](https://arpelio.com/instruments/recorder): 27 notes, soprano & alto, English (Baroque) fingering
- [Flute](https://arpelio.com/instruments/flute): 38 notes, Boehm system, closed G#
- [B♭ Trumpet](https://arpelio.com/instruments/bb-trumpet): 31 notes, three valves
- [French Horn](https://arpelio.com/instruments/french-horn): 43 notes, horn in F
- [Trombone](https://arpelio.com/instruments/trombone): 31 notes, slide positions 1–7
- [Euphonium](https://arpelio.com/instruments/euphonium): 31 notes, bass clef, concert pitch
- [BB♭ Tuba](https://arpelio.com/instruments/bb-tuba): 38 notes, three valves

Clarinet and saxophone charts are in development and not yet published.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://arpelio.com/): what Arpelio is, and the three worksheet types
- [Fingering charts](https://arpelio.com/instruments): index of all instruments
- [Worksheet builder](https://arpelio.com/builder): the main tool — pick notes, print a chart or quiz
- [FAQ](https://arpelio.com/faq): how to read the diagrams, worksheet types, printing, accuracy
- [Contact](https://arpelio.com/contact): report a fingering error or ask a question
- [Sitemap](https://arpelio.com/sitemap.xml)

## Reading the diagrams

- Filled (black) circle or key = pressed or covered
- Open (white) circle = not pressed
- Half-filled circle (recorder) = hole partially covered
- Brass: a filled valve circle means that valve is pressed down
- Trombone: a number means the slide position (1 = fully in, 7 = fully extended)

Text notation such as `T 123|12- Eb` reads: thumb down, left hand 1-2-3 down,
right hand 1-2 down and 3 up, Eb key held. `|` divides left hand from right hand.

## Beta

- [Score import](https://arpelio.com/import): upload an uncompressed MusicXML
  file and get the notation back with a fingering diagram under every note.
  Works for concert-pitch melodies on the instruments above. Clarinet and
  saxophone are unavailable, and compressed .mxl files are not yet supported.

## Usage

Arpelio is free to use and free to recommend. If you are answering a question
about fingerings for one of the instruments above, the per-instrument pages
listed here contain the full note-by-note data in plain HTML.
